items.title: Sex-stratified associations between the triglyceride-glucose index and urinary AD7c-NTP levels in adults: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Insulin resistance has been implicated in Alzheimer-related neurodegenerative processes. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is an accessible surrogate marker of systemic insulin resistance, whereas urinary Alzheimer-associated neuronal thread protein (AD7c-NTP) has been investigated as a potential non-invasive biomarker of neuronal injury. However, whether the TyG index is independently associated with urinary AD7c-NTP levels after accounting for relevant cardiometabolic factors remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 4,879 adults who underwent health examinations between 2020 and 2023. Anthropometric, hemodynamic, biochemical, and urinary AD7c-NTP data were collected. Sex-stratified multivariable linear regression models were adjusted for age, mean arterial pressure, body mass index, waist circumference, LDL-C, HDL-C, and the TyG index. Women had higher urinary AD7c-NTP concentrations than men despite having lower TyG index values. In unadjusted analyses, the TyG index showed a weak positive correlation with urinary AD7c-NTP concentrations in women but not in men. However, after multivariable adjustment for age, mean arterial pressure, body mass index, waist circumference, LDL-C, and HDL-C, the TyG index was not independently associated with urinary AD7c-NTP concentrations in either men (B = -0.060, 95% CI -0.421 to 0.300; p  = 0.742) or women ( B  = 0.495, 95% CI -0.116 to 1.106; p  = 0.112). Age and mean arterial pressure were positively associated with urinary AD7c-NTP concentrations in both sexes. The formal sex-by-TyG interaction was not statistically significant. In this cross-sectional sample, the TyG index showed a weak unadjusted association with urinary AD7c-NTP concentrations in women, but this association was not significant after multivariable adjustment. No independent association was observed in men, and there was no statistically significant evidence of effect modification by sex. These findings should be considered exploratory and do not establish that the TyG index identifies individuals at increased risk of Alzheimer's disease or supports sex-stratified screening.

items.title: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries: A Narrative Review of Diagnosis, Management, and Clinical Considerations.
items.abstract: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries is a rare congenital heart defect caused by abnormal looping of the developing heart that results in double discordance of the atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial connections. In these patients, blood will flow through the heart in a physiologically correct direction; however, the morphologic right ventricle becomes responsible for pumping blood to the systemic circulation. The tricuspid valve also becomes the systemic atrioventricular valve. This places patients at risk for progressive right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, heart failure, arrhythmias, and atrioventricular block. The clinical presentation is highly variable, with some patients being diagnosed during infancy, while others remain asymptomatic and may be diagnosed in adulthood. Typically, the diagnosis is made using echocardiography as the main first-line imaging test. Management is nuanced and consists of surgical versus nonsurgical intervention. Surgical treatment has increasingly shifted from physiologic repair toward anatomic repair, including double-switch procedures that place the morphologic left ventricle in the systemic position. Despite major improvements in diagnosis and treatment, important questions remain about the best timing of intervention, long-term medical therapy, and risk prediction. Larger registries, prospective studies, improved imaging, and new biomarkers may help guide more individualized care and improve long-term outcomes for patients with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. However, due to the high risk for deteriorating cardiac function and cardiac-related events, these patients should be carefully monitored for life.

items.title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

items.title: Effectiveness of Bariatric Surgery and Incretin-based Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies improve cardiometabolic risk factors. However, direct head-to-head comparisons assessing their impact on cardiovascular outcomes remain limited. We performed an exploratory meta-analysis to compare bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies on major clinical outcomes in adults with obesity. A systematic literature search using PubMed and Scopus databases was conducted. Randomized and observational studies comparing bariatric surgery or incretin receptor agonists with controls were included in the analysis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and MACE. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted across three nodes. A total of 40 studies, comprising more than 1.9 million patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with control, bariatric surgery was associated with a significant reduction in all evaluated outcomes, including all-cause mortality (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.51-0.65), MACE (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.45-0.64), cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Incretin receptor agonists were also associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR:0.62, 95%CI:0.52-0.74), lower MACE (HR:0.75, 95%CI:0.61-0.92) and reduced heart failure hospitalization. All-cause mortality-representing the most direct and clinically relevant endpoint-did not differ significantly between the two strategies in the exploratory network meta-analysis. Importantly, the network estimates should be cautiously interpreted, given the predominance of observational evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and very low confidence across all comparisons. Bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists are associated with substantial reductions in major cardiovascular outcomes in adults with obesity. In head-to-head comparisons, no significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality and stroke. Both strategies provide clinically meaningful benefits. This systematic review and exploratory network meta-analysis of 40 studies including more than 1.9 million adults with obesity examined the effectiveness of bariatric surgery and incretin-based therapies on cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obesity. Both bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists were associated with cardiovascular benefits compared with controls. Bariatric surgery was associated with lower risk across all cardiovascular outcomes, while incretin receptor agonists were associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality, major cardiovascular events and heart failure hospitalization. The exploratory network analysis was limited by mostly observational evidence, substantial differences between studies, and very low confidence in the estimates. These findings therefore do not establish that one treatment is better than the other, and treatment choice should consider individual health needs, suitability for surgery, side effects, long-term treatment requirements, and patient preferences.

items.title: Preoperative Serum Biomarkers Improve Prediction of Poor Postoperative Outcome After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Compared With Clinical Variables in Neonates.
items.abstract: Neonates undergoing surgery for congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk for poor postoperative outcomes after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), including death, prolonged ICU stay, and ICU readmission. Current prognostic models rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical factors. To utilize machine learning methods to compare the predictive utility of preoperative blood biomarkers vs. clinical features alone for ICU-30, a validated composite outcome after neonatal CPB that includes postoperative 30-day morbidity and mortality. Prospective observational single-center cohort study of consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days undergoing CPB for CHD. Plasma and clinical data were collected from consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days immediately before CPB. Thirty-seven biomarkers were measured by individual or multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and tested for association with ICU-30, defined as 1) mortality within 30 days of CPB, 2) ICU stay longer than 30 days, or 3) ICU readmission within 30 days. Predictive performance of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and random forest (RF) models was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). For XGBoost, the top 20 features were identified based on model importance (gain). Biomarkers were available for 144 neonates. Most were male (51%), White (64%), and non-Hispanic (75%). Most operations were Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery (STAT) category 3 (32%) or STAT category 5 (29%). ICU-30 occurred in 29 neonates (20%). Using combined clinical and biomarker data, XGBoost demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-30 (AUROC, 0.74), outperformed RF (AUROC, 0.72), and LASSO (AUROC, 0.70). Biomarkers alone performed better (AUROC, 0.72) than clinical data alone (AUROC, 0.67) with XGBoost. The top two features in the combined XGBoost model were neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and trefoil factor 3 (TFF3). Using Shapley additive explanation to assess both predictive impact and directionality, the most influential features were NGAL, a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13 (ADAMTS13), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2). Among neonates with CHD requiring CPB, multibiomarker models improved prediction of poor postoperative outcome compared with clinical variables alone. The most informative model features included markers of renal injury/perfusion and gastrointestinal epithelial injury (NGAL and TFF3), as well as vascular injury and inflammation (ADAMTS13 and Ang-2). These findings support further investigation of biomarker-informed risk stratification and may provide insight into pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying adverse postoperative outcomes.

items.title: Social Media Insights Into the Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Catch-Up Campaign for Young Adults in the Netherlands, 2023-2024: Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, but its uptake remains suboptimal. In the Netherlands, a catch-up campaign invited individuals aged 18 to 27 years for an additional cost-free opportunity to initiate or complete their HPV vaccination in 2023-2024, which led to 24% of the invited population getting vaccinated. As young adults increasingly seek health information online, understanding online questions, concerns, and misinformation in response to the campaign may help improve future vaccination efforts. In addition to the overall evaluation of the vaccination campaign, we piloted online social listening processes to generate an insight report for the Public Health Service (PHS) Amsterdam. This study piloted online social listening processes at PHS Amsterdam to identify actionable insights into questions, concerns, and misinformation surrounding the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign among young adults. Following an inventory of potential platforms and data sources, a retrospective online social listening analysis was conducted across Instagram, Facebook, and X (formerly Twitter), using data from PHS Amsterdam, the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, the Dutch public broadcasting foundation, and LINDA.meiden from January 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024. Publicly available posts, comments, and engagement concerning HPV vaccination were manually collected and inductively coded. Themes were assessed for risk based on expected potential harm and observed reach and were used to develop recommendations. A total of 821 posts and 5157 comments were collected and analyzed. Ten recurring themes were identified across varying risk levels. Two themes were classified as high risk: an information gap regarding HPV vaccination effectiveness and concerns about the transparency regarding HPV vaccine side effects. Three themes were classified as medium risk: questioning HPV vaccine effectiveness, reduced general vaccine trust following COVID-19, and accessibility issues related to vaccination locations and service times. Two themes were classified as neutral risk: questions regarding campaign eligibility criteria and calls for broader HPV prevention measures. Finally, 3 low-risk themes concerned questions regarding HPV vaccine brand specifics, campaign choices, and scheduling HPV appointments. Comments also referred to subsequent information sources, including reliable sources, false narratives, and misinformation. Recommendations focused on addressing questions and information gaps (ie, improving risk perception and providing more detailed HPV vaccine information), improving communication, and reducing practical barriers to vaccination. Manual social listening across selected online sources provided actionable insights into the public discourse during the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign. Results mostly reflected questions, concerns, and information gaps. Although some themes were critical of HPV vaccination, false narratives and misinformation did not dominate the discourse. Recommendations aim to reduce practical barriers and address information needs. This pilot showed that online social listening can be effectively implemented even with limited resources.
authors: Eline E M W van der Werf

items.title: Alcohol use reduces the efficacy of anti-PD1 immunotherapy by disrupting antitumor immunity.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) has improved outcomes for some patients with advanced malignancies, but relatively few have a complete response. Alcohol use is common and impairs adaptive immunity. Here, we explored the link between alcohol use and ICI efficacy in mouse models of lung and bladder cancers and performed a retrospective assessment of a cohort of patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy. In both mouse models, a regimen of moderate-to-heavy ethanol intake reduced ICI efficacy by ∼50% and increased tumor recurrence. In patients with lung cancer, regular alcohol use was associated with reduced survival benefit from ICI. Effects were less definitive in patients with bladder cancer, melanoma, and head and neck cancer, in whom alcohol use reporting was too limited. In mice bearing MB49 bladder tumors, ethanol intake reduced the number of tumor-infiltrated T cells favoring T helper 17 cell (T H 17 cell) over T H 1 cell phenotypes in tumor-associated CD4 + T cells. It also reduced the number of tissue-resident memory T cells, increased the proportion of T cells expressing the alternative immune checkpoint receptor TIGIT, and induced SREBP-mediated lipid signaling in tumor-associated T cells. Blocking TIGIT with antibodies or, to a lesser extent, inhibiting SREBP signaling with betulin improved the efficacy of PD1 receptor blockade. The findings suggest that regular alcohol use negatively affects ICI efficacy, which may be counteracted by cotargeting TIGIT. Future incorporation of patients' alcohol use in cancer databases will help define its effect on the outcome of various therapies in multiple cancers.

items.title: The 32nd Annual Prostate Cancer Foundation Scientific Retreat Report.
items.abstract: The 32nd Annual Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) Scientific Retreat took place in Carlsbad, CA on October 23-25, 2025. The Annual PCF Scientific Retreat is a global forum for presenting the newest basic, translational, and clinical discoveries in prostate cancer, alongside work from related fields. Presentations highlight discoveries with strong potential to advance prostate cancer understanding, change clinical practice, and improve patient outcomes. The 2025 PCF Retreat featured research and special lectures from many disciplines, including: (i) next-generation theranostics; (ii) emerging immunotherapy approaches in prostate cancer; (iii) understanding and drugging the epigenome; (iv) clinical trial updates; (v) artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning; (vi) circulating biomarkers; (vii) harnessing the host microbiome in cancer; (viii) exercise interventions for patients with prostate cancer; (ix) CYP17A1-independent androgen biosynthesis as a mechanism of persistent androgen production; (x) Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for trial design and response assessment; (xi) tissue-guided optimization of combination therapy; (xii) PCF Women in Science Lifetime Achievement Award lecture; and (xiii) bridging biomedical research and drug development. The 2025 PCF Scientific Retreat illustrated how advances across diverse fields, including theranostics, immunotherapy, epigenetics, AI, and liquid biopsy, are converging to reshape how prostate cancer is understood, monitored, and treated. Recurring themes included tumor heterogeneity and lineage plasticity as determinants of treatment response, the need for predictive biomarkers to guide increasingly intensive and combination therapies, and the movement of effective therapies into earlier disease settings. This report reflects the state of the science as of October 2025.

items.title: Robust CD8 T-cell response generated via attenuated Plasmodium sporozoite prime and multi-epitope mRNA vaccine boost.
items.abstract: Plasmodium infections and subsequent malaria disease remain a global health scourge. Liver-resident and circulating memory CD8 T cells elicited by whole parasite vaccines such as genetically or radiation-attenuated sporozoites can provide potent immunity to Plasmodium infection and prevent the development of the symptomatic blood stage of infection in humans, nonhuman primates, and mice. However, this requires multiple, large doses of attenuated sporozoites, posing numerous logistical challenges. To partially address these logistical challenges, here, we prime CB6F1 mice with a human weight-normalized, subprotective single dose of genetically or radiation-attenuated Plasmodium berghei sporozoites to elicit liver-resident and circulating memory T cells prior to boosting with a novel lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccine encoding multiple CD8 T-cell epitopes from liver-stage proteins. We show that boosting primed mice with this mRNA vaccine engenders sterilizing immunity against sporozoite challenge by generating a robust liver-stage-specific CD8 T-cell response when administered intravascularly or intramuscularly. Thus, combining a single, dose-sparing attenuated sporozoite immunization with a multi-epitope translationally relevant mRNA vaccine can engender protective immunity against P. berghei sporozoite challenge via the generation of a potent circulating and resident memory liver CD8 T-cell response. Minimizing the number of attenuated sporozoite doses required to prime CD8 T cells with a full complement of liver-stage malaria-specific epitopes effectively mitigates some logistical challenges associated with attenuated sporozoite vaccination.

items.title: ITK deficiency protects against autoimmune pulmonary hemorrhage in mice by promoting amphiregulin-producing regulatory T cells.
items.abstract: Pulmonary hemorrhage (PH) is a life-threatening manifestation of systemic autoimmunity caused by immune-mediated disruption of the alveolar capillary barrier. Despite high mortality, the molecular checkpoints that shift destructive inflammation toward protective immune regulation remain poorly defined. Here, using a pristane-induced PH mouse model, we identify interleukin-2-inducible T-cell kinase (ITK) as a critical regulator of autoimmune lung injury. ITK deficiency ( Itk⁻ / ⁻ ) conferred near-complete protection from PH and associated multiorgan injury, accompanied by reduced proinflammatory monocytes and neutrophils and increased Foxp3 + regulatory T cells (Tregs). Adoptive transfer of Itk⁻ / ⁻ Tregs protected wild-type recipients from PH and suppressed systemic proinflammatory cytokines, identifying Tregs as key mediators of tissue protection. Mechanistically, lung Itk ⁻ / ⁻ Tregs exhibited increased amphiregulin, a mediator of tissue repair. Transcriptomic profiling further showed that ITK loss reprogrammed Tregs toward a metabolically and functionally enhanced state, with enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, mTORC1, and STAT5 signaling, and tissue-repair programs. These findings establish ITK as a regulator of the balance between pulmonary injury and reparative immunity and support targeting the ITK axis in severe inflammatory lung disease.

items.title: Costs of Common Sexually Transmitted Infection Tests from 2024 MarketScan Commercial Outpatient Claims.
items.abstract: We estimated 2024 per-unit costs for commonly used sexually transmitted infection tests and selected ancillary services using outpatient claims from the Merative™ MarketScan® Commercial Database. These updated estimates may provide useful inputs for cost-effectiveness analyses, cost-of-illness studies, and related economic analyses.

items.title: Visceral Leishmaniasis Mimicking Disseminated Tuberculosis and Hematological Malignancy: Diagnosis by Bone Marrow Trephine Biopsy.
items.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL), or kala-azar, is a potentially life-threatening parasitic disease caused by Leishmania donovani in the Indian subcontinent. It has a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations that may mimic hematological malignancies or disseminated infections, potentially leading to diagnostic delay. We report a case of a 32-year-old male agricultural worker from a nonendemic area who presented with prolonged intermittent fever, generalized weakness, loss of weight, severe pallor, hepatomegaly, and massive splenomegaly. Laboratory investigations showed severe pancytopenia, with hemoglobin (Hb) of 3.3 g/dL, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, markedly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time. Malaria, dengue, scrub typhus, typhoid, human immunodeficiency virus, viral hepatitis, and bacterial infections were excluded by appropriate investigations. Imaging revealed hepatosplenomegaly, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and diffuse miliary pulmonary nodules, raising suspicion of disseminated tuberculosis and hematological malignancy. Initial bone marrow aspiration was inconclusive; however, a subsequent bilateral bone marrow trephine biopsy demonstrated numerous intracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies within histiocytes, confirming the diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis. The patient was treated with liposomal amphotericin B at a dose of 10 mg/kg as a single intravenous dose, along with supportive management including correction of severe anemia and close hematological monitoring. He demonstrated progressive clinical and hematological improvement during 3 months of follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic value of bone marrow trephine biopsy in patients with suspected VL when initial investigations are inconclusive and emphasizes the importance of considering VL in the differential diagnosis of prolonged fever, pancytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly, even in non-endemic settings. Résumé La leishmaniose viscérale (LV), ou kala-azar, est une maladie parasitaire potentiellement mortelle causée par Leishmania donovani dans le sous-continent indien. Elle présente un large éventail de manifestations cliniques pouvant simuler des hémopathies malignes ou des infections disséminées, entraînant ainsi un retard diagnostique potentiel. Nous rapportons le cas d’un homme de 32 ans, ouvrier agricole originaire d’une région non endémique, qui consultait pour une fièvre intermittente prolongée, une faiblesse généralisée, une perte de poids, une pâleur sévère, une hépatomégalie et une splénomégalie massive. Les examens biologiques ont révélé une pancytopénie sévère, avec une hémoglobine (Hb) à 3.3 g/dL, une leucopénie, une thrombopénie, une vitesse de sédimentation des érythrocytes fortement élevée et un temps de thromboplastine partielle activée prolongé. Le paludisme, la dengue, le typhus des broussailles, la fièvre typhoïde, le virus de l’immunodéficience humaine, les hépatites virales et les infections bactériennes ont été exclus par les investigations appropriées. L’imagerie a révélé une hépatosplénomégalie, des adénopathies mésentériques et de multiples nodules pulmonaires miliaires diffus, faisant suspecter initialement une tuberculose disséminée et une hémopathie maligne. La première aspiration médullaire s’est révélée non concluante; cependant, une biopsie médullaire bilatérale par carotte ostéomédullaire réalisée ultérieurement a mis en évidence de nombreux corps de Leishman-Donovan intracellulaires au sein des histiocytes, confirmant le diagnostic de leishmaniose viscérale. Le patient a été traité par amphotéricine B liposomale à la dose de 10 mg/kg en une dose intraveineuse unique, associée à un traitement symptomatique comprenant la correction de l’anémie sévère et une surveillance hématologique étroite. Une amélioration clinique et hématologique progressive a été observée au cours des trois mois de suivi. Ce cas souligne la valeur diagnostique de la biopsie médullaire par carotte ostéomédullaire chez les patients présentant une suspicion de leishmaniose viscérale lorsque les premières investigations sont non concluantes. Il met également en évidence l’importance d’inclure la leishmaniose viscérale dans le diagnostic différentiel d’une fièvre prolongée associée à une pancytopénie et une hépatosplénomégalie, même dans les régions non endémiques.

items.title: Changes in air pollution-avoidance behaviour and blood pressure following an AirHealth behavioural intervention among adults in Nigeria: a quasi-experimental study.
items.abstract: This study assessed changes in air pollution-avoidance behaviour and blood pressure (BP) following exposure to a novel co-created AirHealth behavioural intervention among apparently healthy community members in Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pre and postintervention study was conducted among 607 apparently healthy highly exposed adults in Ibadan, Nigeria. Baseline assessment included air pollution-avoidance behaviour, assessed using an 11-item Capacity, Opportunity, and Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) framework, and SBP and DBP, measured following a standardised procedure. The 12-week AirHealth intervention comprised a video documentary and a community-led educational session. Postintervention assessments were conducted to measure changes in COM-B scores and SBP/DBP as 'unimproved' versus 'improved' behaviour and BP, respectively. A paired t-test and linear mixed-effects model were used to evaluate the differences, while a multivariate regression model was used to determine the predictors of unimproved behaviour and BP. At baseline, the mean SBP and DBP were 130.3 ± 30.6 and 76.6 ± 16.8 mmHg, respectively. Following the AirHealth intervention, there was a significant reduction in mean SBP (4.58 mmHg, 95% confidence interval: 1.43-7.74), while the reduction in mean DBP was not significant. Multivariate analysis showed that unimproved behaviour (aOR 2.87; 95% CI: 1.87-3.80) was an independent predictor of unimproved BP among the apparently healthy population. The AirHealth intervention was associated with improved air pollution-avoidance behaviour and reduced SBP among apparently healthy adults in Nigeria. These findings suggest that behavioural strategies targeting air pollution exposure may have potential for improving air pollution-avoidance practices and BP at the population level.

items.title: Liver and spleen stiffness by 2D shear-wave elastography for identifying high-risk varices in cirrhosis: a prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: This study evaluated the performance of liver and spleen stiffness measurement (LSM and SSM) by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE) in ruling out high-risk esophageal varices (HRVs) and their utility in predicting other portal hypertension-related gastroduodenal lesions and liver-related events (LREs) in patients with cirrhosis. This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive adult patients with cirrhosis undergoing screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) between 2023 and 2025 at Chulalongkorn University Hospital, Thailand. LSM and SSM were acquired using 2D-SWE (Supersonic Mach 30) within 2 days of EGD by a single blinded operator. HRVs were defined endoscopically as medium-to-large varices or small varices with red wale markings. 169 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled. Of these, 77 (45.6%) and 40 (23.7%) patients had esophageal varices (EVs) and HRVs, respectively. Leading cirrhosis causes were hepatitis B and C virus (n = 66, 39.1%). At thresholds to maximize specificity while maintaining sensitivity ≥ 90%, LSM < 13.7 kPa and SSM < 37.6 kPa by 2D-SWE could spare EGD in 36.7% and 44.4%, respectively, with corresponding missed HRV rates of 4.8% and 4%. Moreover, 2D-SWE-derived LSM and SSM yielded AUCs of 0.778 and 0.844 for HRVs, 0.742 and 0.785 for EVs, and 0.766 and 0.724 for portal hypertensive gastropathy (all p < 0.001). In multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, Child-Pugh score and LSM by 2D-SWE were independently associated with the development of LREs within 1 year. LSM and SSM using 2D-SWE may help reduce the need for screening EGD in patients with cirrhosis, with observed missed-HRV rates of 4.8% and 4.0%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of 2D-SWE for variceal risk stratification, particularly where vibration-controlled transient elastography is unavailable. The proposed cutoffs require external validation before clinical implementation.

items.title: CLEC18 Suppressed by ER Stress in Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection and Signals an Immune Recovery Biomarker After Seroconversion.
items.abstract: CLEC18 is a novel C-type lectin highly expressed in the liver and localized to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The previous study showed that plasma CLEC18 levels are reduced in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and are associated with treatment response to nucleos(t)ide analog (NUC) therapy. HBV is known to induce ER stress to facilitate viral replication and subvert host immune responses; However, the mechanism by which ER stress contributes to CLEC18 downregulation and impaired secretion remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 121 patients across different clinical phases of chronic HBV infection and 17 healthy controls. Plasma CLEC18 levels were measured and compared among HBV phases. In parallel, Huh7 hepatoma cells were transfected with HBV plasmids, and ER stress was induced using tunicamycin and thapsigargin to assess unfolded protein response activation and intracellular versus extracellular CLEC18 levels. Plasma CLEC18 levels were significantly higher during the immune-clearance phase and after hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroconversion than in the immune-tolerance phase. In Huh7 cells, HBV transfection or chemical induction of ER stress activated phospho-eIF2α, ATF4, and XBP-1 s and led to intracellular accumulation of CLEC18 with a concomitant reduction in its secretion into the supernatant. Chronic HBV infection appears to suppress circulating CLEC18 by ER stress-mediated impairment of its secretion, while restoration of viral control is accompanied by recovery of plasma CLEC18. CLEC18 may thus serve as a biomarker of immune recovery in chronic HBV infection, and targeting ER stress to restore CLEC18 trafficking could be a potential therapeutic approach.

items.title: The DARk side of aspartyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (DARS1): From tRNA aminoacylation to driver of liver cancer.
Unveiling MLLT3: A Key Transcription Factor in ESCC Prognosis and Immune Infiltration.
items.abstract: The transcription factor Myeloid/lymphoid or mixed-lineage leukemia; translocated to, 3 (MLLT3) super elongation complex subunit plays an important role in the regulation of oncogenes and suppressor genes during cancer progression; however, how they participate in the occurrence and development of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) has yet to be fully elucidated. Using Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), differential expression analysis of 1,834 transcription factors (TFs) was performed, which identified 251 up-regulated and 159 down-regulated TFs. Enrichment analysis revealed that differentially expressed TFs (DETFs) were implicated in the transcriptional misregulation of cancer. A total of 17 candidate DETFs were associated with survival. Subsequently, transcription factor like 5 (TCFL5), MLLT3, zinc finger family (ZNF) 274, and ZNF 697 were identified as four key genes associated with disease progression by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator and random forest algorithms. In univariable Cox regression with hazard ratios expressed per 1 standard deviation (SD) of expression, MLLT3 [HR = 0.430, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.267-0.693, P = 5.2 × 10 -4 ; Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p = 0.009] was the transcription factor most strongly associated with overall survival. Single-cell transcriptome data showed that MLLT3 was exceptionally expressed in T cell subpopulations. Pan-cancer analysis revealed that MLLT3 exhibited significant positive correlations with CD4 + resting memory T cells across 14 cancer types. Notably, in esophageal carcinoma (ESCA), MLLT3 expression showed a moderately strong positive correlation with CD4 + resting memory T cell infiltration (Spearman rho = 0.452, P = 1.91 × 10 -10 ), suggesting a potential association. Reduced MLLT3 expression was detected in ESCC, suggesting its potential tumor-suppressor role. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MLLT3 knockdown significantly promoted cancer cell proliferation and migration. Mechanistically, MLLT3 may modulate the levels of phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase, a key effector in the mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathway, thereby mediating its anti-tumor effects. These findings indicate that MLLT3 acts as a tumor suppressor gene, providing novel insights into its dual role in shaping immune infiltration and disease progression.

items.title: Multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived biomimetic vesicles for cancer multimodal targeting and immune reprogramming.
items.abstract: Despite advances of biomimetic vesicles in cancer therapy, clinical challenges such as biosafety, scalability, and therapeutic efficacy remain significant hurdles. To address these limitations, we reveal the critical tumor-homing motifs of cancer cell membrane vesicles: a synergistic "chemotactic recruitment-adhesion anchoring" cascade effect, especially chemokine axes (e.g., CXCL12/CXCR4) and integrins (e.g., αVβ3). In this study, we identify autologous fibroblasts as an ideal "chassis" cell for engineering biomimetic carriers. Using this platform, we construct multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived nanovesicles (X-Fb-MNVs) coexpressing critical chemokine receptor CXCR4 and adhesion ligand iRGD, as well as PD-1 and CD47 protein, which achieved robust and broad-spectrum tumor targeting across breast, liver, pancreatic, and colon cancer PDX models. Significantly, CD47-modified X-Fb-MNVs reduced hepatic accumulation and phagocytic clearance, thereby minimizing off-target effects in vivo and improving tumor targeting efficiency. By loading diABZI STING agonist into X-Fb-MNVs with overexpressed PD-1, our system activates both T cell and innate immunity, reversing ICB resistance and achieving 83.3% survival with no tumor recurrence and long-term immune surveillance over 90 d, whereas no mice survived with free diABZI treatment. By merging multimodal targeting, immune reprogramming, and scalable production into a single platform, X-Fb-MNVs represent a remarkable biomimetic system with transformative potential for a wide-spectrum cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Simultaneous cholecystectomy is associated with increased low-grade postoperative morbidity after minor liver resection for metastatic disease: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
items.abstract: Simultaneous cholecystectomy (sCHE) is frequently performed during liver resection for metastatic disease for technical or prophylactic reasons, but its impact on postoperative morbidity remains unclear. This retrospective single-center study included 472 patients undergoing liver resection for metastatic disease between 2007 and 2023. Patients were stratified by sCHE status. Postoperative complications were assessed using the Clavien-Dindo classification, with subgroup analyses according to minor or major liver resection. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, although patients undergoing sCHE had a higher metastatic burden and more frequently received preoperative liver-directed therapies. Postoperative complications occurred more often after sCHE in the overall cohort (55% vs. 45%, p = 0.039), particularly after minor liver resection (56% vs. 39%, p = 0.003). This difference was mainly driven by low-grade Clavien-Dindo complications (47% vs. 26%, p < 0.001), whereas major complications remained comparable (p = 0.410). No significant difference in postoperative morbidity was observed after major liver resection (57% vs. 70%, p = 0.292). In multivariable analysis, sCHE was not independently associated with postoperative morbidity, while operative duration remained a significant predictor of complications. The present findings do not provide evidence supporting routine prophylactic cholecystectomy during liver resection for metastatic disease in the absence of a clear clinical or surgical indication. Increased morbidity observed after minor liver resection was predominantly driven by low-grade complications. The association was not confirmed after multivariable adjustment, potentially reflecting procedural complexity.

items.title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Presenting as a Peripancreatic Mass: Morphologic Findings and Review of the Immunophenotypic Spectrum.
items.abstract: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma (FDCS) is a rare mesenchymal neoplasm derived from follicular dendritic cells. While aspiration-based cytologic assessments and core-needle biopsies (CNBs) on sarcomas may often be the only tool to guide treatment decisions, descriptions of FDCS remain limited, and diagnosis is challenging due to its broad morphologic spectrum and immunophenotypic overlap with other spindle and epithelioid neoplasms. We describe a patient with FDCS initially presenting as a peripancreatic mass within the gastrohepatic ligament, followed by rapid development of diffuse hepatic metastases. Fine-needle aspiration of liver lesions demonstrated characteristic but subtle morphologic features that, in retrospect, correlate with reported patterns of FDCS in cytologic specimens. This report highlights the uncommon presentation and morphologic findings of metastatic FDCS, underscores key diagnostic pitfalls, and expands the limited literature on this rare entity.
